transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep having thoughts that it might be better if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes I feel like dying would be some kind of fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and the people I work with.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time?
I’m not sure how to answer that. I know I haven’t felt right, but “sad or empty most of the time”… I guess I’d need to think about what you mean by that.
Do you feel sad most of the time?
I don’t know if I’d call it sad most of the time. I feel bad a lot, but I’m not sure how to separate that from just feeling worn down.
Do you find pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Not really. I used to paint, and I liked cooking big meals, and I’d run before jobs sometimes. I used to show up for theater rehearsals too. Now all of that just feels like chores from somebody else’s life. I don’t really care if I miss it.
Do you often feel guilty?

Yes. A lot. I keep thinking everything that went wrong is because of me—like my husband getting worse, the crew losing work, clients’ homes getting messed up. It feels like I ruin whatever I touch, and sometimes I think I deserve whatever happens to me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband got hurt, and it just kind of stayed.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to find enjoyable?

Yeah. Like I said, I used to actually enjoy painting, cooking big meals, going for runs before work, even theater rehearsals. Now it all just feels like something I’m supposed to do, not something I want to do. Like it belongs to somebody else’s life, and I don’t really care if I miss any of it.
Have you had any periods in the past two weeks where you felt better for a few days?
Not really, no. It’s been pretty constant. This has been hanging over me for about a year and two months now, since a few months after my husband got hurt.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would give you pleasure?

Yeah. I don’t really get pleasure from those things anymore. Painting, cooking a big meal, going for a run before a job, even theater rehearsals… they all just feel like chores now. Like they’re from somebody else’s life, and I don’t really care if I miss them.
Have you had any episodes in the past where you felt this way, and then it went away for a while before coming back?
Not really in that kind of on-and-off way. This has mostly just been with me steadily for about a year and two months, since a few months after my husband got injured.
Are these feelings you've been having usually present for most of the day?
Yeah, most of the day. It’s kind of just there when I wake up and it stays with me. It’s been like that for a long time now—about a year and two months, since a few months after my husband got hurt.
Have you had any periods in the past year where you felt completely back to normal?

No, not completely back to normal. Some weeks have been a little less crushing, I guess, but most of the time the guilt, the exhaustion, not caring about things, and those thoughts about death have still been there.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling this way in your life?
I don’t think so. Not like this. I’ve had hard times before, but this feels like one long stretch rather than separate episodes.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight over the past year?
Yeah. I’ve lost some weight, I think. I’m not trying to, but most days I either forget to eat until really late or I’ll take a few bites and feel kind of sick. My work pants have gotten loose.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you didn't feel this way since it started?

No, I don’t think I’ve had two months where it really lifted. It’s been going on about a year and two months now, since a few months after my husband got injured. Some days are a little better than others, but it hasn’t gone away for that long.
Have you had any periods where these feelings completely went away before returning?

No, not really. It’s been there pretty much the whole time, for about a year and two months now, since a few months after my husband got hurt. It might ease up some days, but it hasn’t completely gone away and then come back.
Do you find that your feelings of guilt, exhaustion, or not caring about things tend to worsen or improve at specific times of the year?
I haven’t really noticed a seasonal pattern. It doesn’t seem like it’s worse in winter or better in summer or anything like that. It’s more just been there most of the time.
Do you think you've lost the ability to find pleasure in things that used to be enjoyable to you?

Yes. I used to really enjoy painting, cooking big meals, going for runs before jobs, and showing up for theater rehearsals. Now all of that feels like chores from somebody else’s life. I just… don’t care if I miss them anymore.
Have you ever felt this way before this episode started about a year and two months ago?
No, not like this. This has really been going on for about a year and two months, starting a few months after my husband got injured. Before that, I don’t remember feeling this way for this long.
Have you had any other episodes like this before the one that started a year and two months ago?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember having another stretch like this before. Not one that stands out the way this past year has.
